contents.name: Chapter 1, Introductory Ideas and Examples
contents.reason: This chapter applies generating functions to recurrence solving and multivariate counting rather than developing the coefficientwise algebra of formal series; those applications belong to the downstream recurrence and enumerative-combinatorics pages.

contents.name: Section 1.1, An easy two term recurrence
contents.reason: The worked first-order recurrence and its rational generating function are application material for linear-recurrences-and-rational-generating-functions, while the present pair supplies the formal ring operations used there.

contents.name: Section 1.2, A slightly harder two term recurrence
contents.reason: This recurrence-solving example depends on rational-function decomposition and coefficient recovery, the central topic of linear-recurrences-and-rational-generating-functions rather than a missing prerequisite for formal-series algebra.

contents.name: Section 1.3, A three term recurrence
contents.reason: The Fibonacci recurrence calculation is reserved for linear-recurrences-and-rational-generating-functions; repeating it here would pre-empt that page instead of strengthening the present formal definitions or theorems.

contents.name: Section 1.4, A three term boundary value problem
contents.reason: The boundary-value recurrence is a specific generating-function application whose natural home is linear-recurrences-and-rational-generating-functions, not an algebraic result needed by the current pair.

contents.name: Section 1.5, Two independent variables
contents.reason: Bivariate generating functions and their coefficient applications belong to the later enumerative-combinatorics developments; the present page deliberately defines and proves the one-variable formal-series machinery they will use.

contents.name: Section 1.6, Another 2-variable case
contents.reason: The Stirling- and Bell-number bivariate calculations belong to set-partitions-stirling-numbers-and-exponential-generating-functions, whose topic includes the counting structures absent from this algebraic page.

contents.name: Theorem 1.6.1, exponential generating function of the Bell numbers
contents.reason: The Bell-number exponential generating function is a principal result for set-partitions-stirling-numbers-and-exponential-generating-functions; this page supplies formal exponentials but does not duplicate that later counting theorem.

contents.name: Chapter 2, Series
Section 2.1, Formal power series

Section 2.1 proposition, a compositional inverse of a zero-constant series must have nonzero linear coefficient
Section 2.1 proposition, a formal series with zero derivative is constant
Section 2.1 proposition, $f'=f$ implies $f=ce^x$
Section 2.2, The calculus of formal ordinary power series generating functions
Rule 1, sequence shifts correspond to removal of initial coefficients and division by a power of $x$
contents.reason: The rule is recurrence-solving machinery used systematically on linear-recurrences-and-rational-generating-functions; the current coefficient-extraction proposition supplies the algebra but does not duplicate the application calculus.

contents.name: Rule 2, polynomial functions of the index correspond to polynomial functions of $xD$
Rule 3, products of ordinary generating functions give Cauchy convolution
Rule 4, coefficients of a positive integer power are finite multi-index convolutions
Rule 5, division by $1-x$ generates partial sums
contents.reason: Partial-sum transformations are an application of the geometric inverse on linear-recurrences-and-rational-generating-functions; the present B page proves the underlying formal geometric identity without repeating that application.

contents.name: Section 2.3, The calculus of formal exponential generating functions
contents.reason: The labelled-product convolution and exponential-generating-function calculus are developed with their counting meaning on set-partitions-stirling-numbers-and-exponential-generating-functions, not on this one-variable algebra page.

contents.name: Rules 1′–3′, shifts, polynomial index weights, and binomial convolution for exponential generating functions
contents.reason: These rules require the labelled counting interpretation assigned to set-partitions-stirling-numbers-and-exponential-generating-functions; retaining only formal exponential identities here keeps the page boundary exact.

contents.name: Section 2.4, Power series, analytic theory
Theorem 2.4.1, radius of convergence from the coefficient-root limit superior
Theorem 2.4.2, analyticity inside the circle of convergence and a singularity on its boundary
contents.reason: The complex-analytic singularity statement uses analytic continuation and Cauchy estimates rather than formal algebra; it belongs to the complex-analysis track and is not a prerequisite for any retained formal theorem.

contents.name: Theorem 2.4.3, nearest-singularity bounds on coefficient growth
contents.reason: Coefficient asymptotics from complex singularities are analytic-combinatorics machinery, while this pair deliberately proves only coefficientwise formal identities and does not use analytic convergence.

contents.name: Section 2.5, Some useful power series
Section 2.6, Dirichlet series, formal theory
contents.reason: Formal Dirichlet series encode multiplicative number-theoretic functions with Dirichlet convolution, a different algebraic object from $R[[x]]$ and not machinery needed by the assigned downstream combinatorics pages.

contents.name: Theorem 2.6.1, Euler product for a multiplicative arithmetic function
contents.reason: The Euler-product identity belongs to multiplicative number theory and depends on prime factorisation rather than ordinary Cauchy multiplication; no result in this pair uses it.
